question.text: Meridian Capital (Cat II) is appointing a Merchant Banker for a new scheme launch. Which of the following appointments is PROHIBITED under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Appointing an MB that previously advised another unrelated Cat II fund
Appointing a domestic MB (vs an offshore bank)
Appointing an MB that is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the fund's Sponsor — i.e., an ASSOCIATE of the AIF's sponsor/manager/trustee
Appointing the same MB for PPM filing and ongoing annual PPM audit

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, a Merchant Banker appointed by the fund shall NOT be an associate of the AIF, its sponsor, manager or trustee. A wholly-owned subsidiary of the Sponsor qualifies as an associate — hence this appointment is prohibited. Independence of the MB safeguards PPM due-diligence integrity. The Trap: Serving other unrelated AIFs is normal MB practice. Domestic MBs are permitted (and most common). The PPM-audit distractor misleads — PPM audit is done by a practising CA/CS under a separate mandate, NOT by the MB; PPM AUDIT is a separate regulated function. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests MB associate-prohibition. III-A/III-C tests associate definitions across SEBI intermediaries. XV (Research Analyst) tests research-IB chinese wall — adjacent concept. Manager's Pro-Tip: Maintain a SEBI-verified MB independence certificate on file at every PPM filing — SEBI inspection can retroactively challenge MB-associate relationships. Also factor MB fee structure into set-up cost caps in the PPM.
